findings.title: Migration can crash when expected site setting rows do not exist
findings.body: The migration indexes directly into the first row of raw SQL results: execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i. On fresh installs, or on sites where embed_category was never changed, the site_settings row will not exist, so [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError. The same unsafe pattern is used at line 15 for uncategorized_category_id. This can block the migration completely.

A stored value containing a single quote or SQL fragment can break the migration or execute unintended SQL. These values should be inserted through parameterized SQL or at least connection.quote.

findings.title: Existing embeddable hosts are migrated without normalization
findings.body: The migration copies old embeddable_hosts lines verbatim into embeddable_hosts.host. The new model only strips scheme and path in an ActiveRecord before_validation callback, which migrations bypass. Existing values like http://example.com, https://example.com/path, or blank lines will be stored as-is or as empty rows. Since EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later compares only the URI host against lower(host), these migrated rows may never match, silently breaking embedding after upgrade.

findings.title: before_validation mutates host without guarding against nil
findings.body: EmbeddableHost's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! unconditionally. If host is nil, for example from a malformed admin API request, this raises NoMethodError before validations can run. The callback should guard against blank/nil host, and the model should have an explicit presence validation.

TopicEmbed.import later uses EmbeddableHost#category_id when creating topics, so invalid category references can cause data integrity problems or failed topic creation.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint or validation on host

EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses where(...).first without an order, so if duplicates exist with different categories, the category used for imported topics is arbitrary.

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port will never match incoming referers
findings.body: The host validation regex allows an optional port, so example.com:8080 can be saved. However record_for_host parses the incoming URL with URI and compares only uri.host, which excludes the port. As a result, a configured host with a port will never match http://example.com:8080/, making port-specific host entries unusable.

findings.title: Plural embedded ID hydration can create undefined records or throw
findings.body: _hydrateEmbedded assumes any key ending in _ids is an array and calls obj[k].map. If the payload contains null or undefined for that key, this throws. If some IDs cannot be found via _lookupSubType, the resulting association array contains undefined entries, and the original *_ids key is deleted anyway. UI code iterating that association may then fail.

If the selected category was blank and the server normalized it to the uncategorized category, or if the local categoryId is undefined, the UI may display the wrong category or no category. It should use the category_id returned in the saved host payload.

findings.title: resources :embeddable_hosts exposes routes with no controller actions

Requests to the extra routes will result in missing action errors. The route should be restricted to only the implemented actions.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding does not update anything
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddingController#update ignores all request parameters and simply renders the current embedding object. The client defines a saveChanges action that issues this update, but the endpoint cannot persist any embedding-level changes. If no attributes are intended to be editable here, the route/action should be removed or the endpoint should be implemented.
